messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release/2026-03-15 (canary group A, us-west-2). Automated checks flagged a spike in 5xxs ~3 minutes after rollout. rolling:hold applied by deploy system. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: PAGERDUTY -> oncall @maya (P1) — observed 5xx spike + increased tail latency for inference API. Please acknowledge with /incident ack.

maya: ack. jumping in. looking at traces/logs now.

maya: quick triage — error class = downstream runtime OOM + kv-cache eviction errors. spike correlates exactly with commit 1a2b3c4 (model cache prefetch change). reproduced locally on staging with a short traffic replay.

kevin: that commit landed in the canary subset only. I can revert it. prepping a revert patch.

kevin: command I'm running: ```bash
git checkout -b hotfix/revert-1a2b3c4
git revert 1a2b3c4 -m 1
git push origin hotfix/revert-1a2b3c4
# open PR and bypass non-blocking checks with admin merge if needed
```

sarah: PR #1245 created by kevin: "hotfix: revert cache prefetch commit 1a2b3c4" — adding maya and ops for review. skipping long-running perf tests for canary-only rollback. :thumbsup:

maya: also enable feature-flag kill for safety: flag `enable_kv_prefetch` -> off for all deployments. Ops, can you flip it and confirm?

ops-bot: feature flag toggle request acknowledged. Executing: `POST /flags/toggle {"flag":"enable_kv_prefetch","state":false}` against flags API. Response: 200 OK. Flag now OFF for canary and prod. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: starting canary hotfix rollout: deploying hotfix/revert-1a2b3c4 to canary group A (batch size 10%). watching metrics.

support-bot: notifying customer-facing channels. Sending templated alert to 3 affected customers and to account execs. Message: "We observed transient increased error rates during a canary deploy; mitigation in progress. No data exposure. Will update soon."

maya: metrics update after hotfix push + flag kill: 5xx rate down from ~42% in canary to <1.2% in 3 minutes. Latency P95 back to baseline. Looks like rollback + flag kill fixed it.

jon: I'm coming up on shift at 19:10 UTC — maya handing over. Summary for handoff: root cause = aggressive kv-cache prefetch causing memory growth and OOMs in some runtime shards; scope = canary group A, spilled to a tiny fraction of production traffic due to routing overlap; mitigation = revert commit 1a2b3c4 + kill feature flag; current status = canary healthy, metrics stable.

maya: impact estimate: ~3 premium customers saw elevated error rates (we already messaged them). rough total request impact ~0.2% of overall traffic during the 6-minute window. No retries or secondary failures observed in downstream services.

kevin: created follow-up tasks: #ENG-789 add memory regression tests, #ENG-790 add alert on per-instance cache memory delta, #OPS-456 run canary isolation check to avoid routing bleed.

maya: handing control to @jon. I'll be available on thread for any follow-ups. Recommend postmortem and retro to cover test coverage and canary scale policy.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED by maya at 19:12 UTC. Please file a postmortem within 72 hours and link to this thread.

jon: acknowledged. I will own the postmortem and the follow-ups. tagging eng-rt and eng-sre. :raised_hands:
